name: Evaporative cooling tower

sources.title: Delta Cooling Towers: how to calculate water loss in a cooling tower

summary: Water is sprayed through fill while fans pull air across it; evaporation cools the rest of the water to a few kelvin above wet-bulb. The most compact and efficient heat rejection, but it evaporates about 1.5 L per kWh plus blowdown.

approachK.note: Approach to wet-bulb; ~4 K is the nominal design for large data-center towers (ASHRAE practice), 2.5 K possible with oversized fill. Excludes an isolating plate heat exchanger (another 1 to 2 K).

fanPowerFraction.note: Induced-draft tower fans run about 0.03 to 0.09 kW per ton of heat rejected (0.008 to 0.025 W/W).

waterLPerKwh.note: Evaporation: 3.6 MJ per kWh / 2.43 MJ/kg latent heat at ~30 °C = 1.48 kg. Some heat leaves as sensible air heating (lower), while drift adds 0.001 to 0.2% of circulation (higher). Blowdown is added with towerBlowdownFactor.

unitCapacityW.note: Typical factory-assembled or field-erected cell size for data-center plants.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Tower cells, plate heat exchanger and water treatment; cheapest per kW of the four because evaporation shrinks the equipment.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Modular factory-built cells are faster than chillers; no primary 2025 figure found.

installWeeks.note: Basin, piping, water treatment and controls.

footprintM2PerMw.note: Evaporative towers reject several times more heat per square metre than dry coils.
